title: Mint mode does not roll back on partial failure
position: Run mode revokes succeeded credentials when one provider fails. Mint mode returns an error and does not revoke. This asymmetry is intended behaviour, not a defect.
rationale: Ben ratified the asymmetry on 2026-08-18 during backtrace decision review (decision key mint_mode_rollback). Mint mode prints no partial output, and the TTL bound limits the life of any leaked credential. A future change may still add mint rollback as new work.

title: The refresh subsystem ships
position: The refresh subsystem stays in the product. The rewrite must wire it to a live command path. Its twelve landed obligations describe required behaviour, not abandoned design.
rationale: Ben decided to keep the feature on 2026-08-18 during backtrace decision review (decision key refresh_subsystem_fate). The refresh obligations landed as proposals with the unwired caveat and remain discoverable when rewrite work touches their evidence paths.

title: Revocation is identifier-only
position: A revoke command receives the credential identifier and the provider name only. The provider contract drops NOSCOPE_TOKEN as a value channel. A provider that needs the credential value to revoke is unsupported. The token-carrying library revoke path must be deleted in the rewrite.
rationale: Ben chose identifier-only on 2026-08-18 (decision key revoke_contract_choice). The binary already behaves this way, RevokeInput makes a credential-carrying revoke unconstructible, and identifier-only matches the no-secrets-in-flight posture of NS-012. This supersedes the NS-038 draft contract half that promised a real NOSCOPE_TOKEN value.
